thread:
Alex: quick kickoff for a Karpenter GPU canary. focus: ENI/IP density guardrails, safe drains for long-running training, and consolidation impact on pod churn. keeping it single-AZ to limit blast radius.

Sara: sounds good. can you drop a concise checklist + the concrete metrics we want recorded?

Alex: checklist (short):
1) Scope: single AZ, 2 provisioners (spot-prefer, ondemand-fallback), max 24 GPUs.
2) Workloads: 2 x long-training, 8 x short-batch, 3 x interactive debug.
3) Metrics to record: pod_start_ms, node_boot_ms, gpu_alloc_latency_ms, eni_per_instance, eni_usage_pct_per_az, device_plugin_restarts, containerd_restarts, pod_eviction_rate.
4) Drain behavior: preStop in containers + node pre-terminate hook that verifies zero allocs and MIG cleanup. test forced kills and device-plugin flaps.
5) Consolidation: run conservative for first 2 hours, then toggle aggressive for 45m to observe drift.
6) Safety gates: auto-pause consolidation if eni_usage_pct >= 82% per-AZ OR pod_eviction_rate > 4%/hr.
7) Rollback: label provisioner paused=true and fail heavy jobs back to Dedicated pool.

Mike: add kernel / driver restarts to the metric list. last time a driver restart preceded many evictions. also want a chaos test that kills device-plugin and then tries to schedule a GPU pod on the same node.

Julia: cost caveat: fewer larger instances lowers VM overhead but raises per-termination impact on many pods and increases IP demand per node. capture $/GPU-hour, expected pod-loss-per-spot-termination. include sensitivity for spot churn.

Alex: pre-terminate hook idea: wait for device-plugin to report 0 allocations and for MIG cleanup marker file. example snippet below (heuristic):

```
#!/bin/bash
NODE="$1"
kubectl cordon "$NODE"
# poll device-plugin status until no allocs or timeout
for i in {1..24}; do
  allocs=$(kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l app=nvidia-device-plugin -o jsonpath='{.items[*].status.containerStatuses[*].state}' 2>/dev/null || true)
  if [[ -z "$allocs" || "$allocs" == *"terminated"* ]]; then
    break
  fi
  sleep 5
done
# optional MIG cleanup check
if [ -f /var/run/mig-cleanup-done ]; then
  sleep 2
fi
kubectl drain "$NODE" --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

Sara: good. i will add dashboards and alerts: ENI usage per AZ, node_launch_latency, pod_eviction_rate, gpu_alloc_latency, device_plugin_restart_count. alert: eni_usage_pct >=82% -> webhook to ops-oncall and runbook trigger.

infra-bot: created canary: `canary/karpenter-gpu-eni-guard` window Fri 02:00-08:00 UTC. CI job: ci/karpenter/gpu-eni-guard-canary.

Mike: chaos plan: 1) SIGKILL device-plugin on node A then attempt scheduling; 2) simulate kubelet OOM and observe if karpenter tries to replace node with allocated GPUs; 3) simulate spot termination notice for a large instance and ensure graceful migration/eviction. record pod-loss and time-to-recover.

Sara: automation: add a controller-run alerting webhook that will run a command to label the provisioner `paused=true` when eni_usage_pct >=82% and send a Slack pm to ops.ops-oncall.

Ops-Oncall: i'll monitor the window. my manual mitigation is `kubectl label provisioner/gpu-eni-guard paused=true` and then coordinate failover. have runbook open.

Julia: i'll produce a compact cost model by Wed: compare 1) many small gpus, 2) fewer larger instances, 3) mixed with instance selection skewed to high-ENI-density types. include pod-churn risk and expected savings.

Alex: provisioner YAML defaults to include ttlSecondsAfterEmpty and consolidation enabled. recommended conservative snippet for canary:

```
apiVersion: karpenter.sh/v1alpha5
kind: Provisioner
metadata:
  name: gpu-eni-guard
spec:
  ttlSecondsAfterEmpty: 600
  consolidation:
    enabled: true
  requirements:
  - key: karpenter.sh/capacity-type
    operator: In
    values: [spot, on-demand]
```

Mike: also set a soft node-label based preference for instance types with >4 ENIs per vcpu equivalent. helps reduce AZ-level IP pressure.

Sara: owners & next steps:
- Alex: finalize YAML + pre-terminate script and push to infra repo.
- Sara: dashboards, ENI alert webhook and auto-pause integration.
- Mike: implement chaos tests + device-plugin kill and kubelet-failure cases.
- Julia: cost sims and sensitivity analysis.

Alex: timeline: infra-bot scheduled the window for Fri. i'll publish final playbook + rollback steps by Tue EOD. flag objections here now. :eyes:
